Timothy — thanks for the packet and the clear asks. Quick readback and a few clarifying questions below. We're looping in Marissa and Jonas for acceptance criteria and the canary plan.

Readback (short):
- Control plane: propose split control-plane routers in a redundant pair inside the customer rack, mirrored to our control-plane relay in the colo. Control-plane heartbeats will use the private management VLAN, not the public egress path.
- Data plane: inference nodes sit behind a local edge load balancer; egress to internet flows through Arkadia-managed NAT boxes. BGP will be used for WAN failover; local route preferences will steer traffic to MPLS when primary is down.
- KV cache promotion: we will warm the secondary and route traffic via a weighted shift — expect transient token latency but aim for <250ms for active sessions.

Clarifying questions:
1) Can Arkadia provide the control-plane management VLAN CIDR and the expected MTU for the fabric? That affects our sidecar and tunnel MTU settings.
2) On the egress ACLs — do you allow ephemeral high ports outbound for health-check callbacks (tcp/1024-65535)? If not, we need a static port mapping for our observability callbacks.

Next steps:
- Jonas: can you validate the BGP MED/local-pref behavior required to hit the failover goals?
- Marissa: I'll hand the canary acceptance checklist to you for pricing/operational constraints and evidence requirements.

I'll be available for a 30-min call at 11:30 PT if that works for you, Timothy.

Cheers,

On Tue, May 28, 2028 at 10:03 AM Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com> wrote:
> Quick readback and a few clarifying questions below.

Quick technical notes / validation items from me:

- BGP failover: the proposed approach (local-pref -> MED -> AS-path) is fine. For the <=200ms target on user-visible requests you will need: rapid BFD sessions between Arkadia edge and our relay (min 50ms timers), and an active session drainage strategy on the edge LB. Expect the BGP convergence window to be ~100-300ms with BFD + ECMP removed.

- KV cache promotion: to hit <250ms, we need KV cache warmup to be pre-seeded and a fast in-memory snapshot transfer. I recommend a staged promotion: (1) pre-warm to replica, (2) switch the active pointer in <50ms, (3) allow 1s of tail-latency smoothing. We'll document exact observability hooks.

- NAT/eACLs: if Arkadia restricts ephemeral outbound ports, we must negotiate a static egress port range for our health and telemetry callbacks (as Chloe noted). Also confirm whether DNAT will be used for incoming admin access or if access will be via bastion. Our preference is bastion + jumpbox (mTLS).

Action items I will take:
- Produce a short 1-pager on BFD/BGP timers and recommended LB drain settings (will attach to the runbook).
- List of exact ports/protocols Redwood needs for deployment and ongoing telemetry.

I'll attach the BGP timers doc to the final runbook and feed into the canary checklist.

Jonas Weber
Sr. Network Architect | Redwood Inference

- Success criteria: 1) KV promotion completes with <250ms service interruption for active sessions (measured via synthetic probe), 2) WAN failover occurs with recovery <300ms as measured by BFD/BGP timers, 3) No telemetry loss for >99.9% of events in the 10m window during failover.
- Evidence pack: network pcap snippets, BFD session logs, synthetic probe traces, runbook checklist (onprem-resiliency-runbook-draft.md).

Operational asks for Arkadia:
- Provide management VLAN CIDR and confirm MTU + whether GENEVE GRE is permitted.
